en: Come, let him hear the story of the sacrifice of Bismillah—
the great one who offered his own immortal self as a libation for the welfare of the motherland,
born in the city of Shahjahampur in the house of Pandit Muralidhar.
Bismillah, who had been protected, nourished, and raised by his mother Mūlamatī,
and who had met with Somadeva Svāmin as a spiritual preceptor for his life,
was moved by the suffering of India’s plight and felt a sense of obligation toward him.
Having planted the seed of his resolve upon the earth, he made a firm vow that you should come and hear his story; thus, at the time of Bismillah’s sacrifice,
he went to the Lakhnau assembly and joined the gathering.
Having become a rebel, he was honored there by Virāṭa with a ceremonial mark (tilaka);
he engaged in deep reflection and deliberation with the members of the Anuśīlana Committee, and the constitution of the Hindustānī Praja-tantra Saṅgha was drafted.
Having been carefully prepared for the commencement of the invasion of Iraq,
Bismillah Balidān came to hear the news;
he was stationed underground within Mainpuri Sadhankaran during the rainy season.
Many books were composed by him; even as time passed,
he observed the distress of his family members after the gift of forgiveness,
and Bismillah returned once more to his own city, Shahjahampur, where he resided at home.
Because of his concern for the maintenance and nourishment of his household, he has set out on a journey;
he has come to hear the word of the offering of Bismillah.
Where has sleep gone? Perhaps it has come to the hero. Most of them have arrived.
No one made any effort regarding this matter because their work was already accomplished; however,
upon hearing the news of the suspension of the non-cooperation movement,
a profound sense of disillusionment arose in Bismillah’s heart toward Gandhi.
He had left his home, yet he was found again on the road as he was traveling;
he came to hear the story of Bismillah’s sacrifice.
He was sought after, but the steadfast, virtuous, and noble youth remained hidden in the branches.
Vigorous through his poetry, that fire blazed within his heart;
having delivered his speech in the midst of the assembly, he created an atmosphere that constructed a framework for a democratic union in every province.
The revolutionaries from among the youth of proclaimed India have come to hear the story of Bismillah’s sacrifice from you;
it has been composed by himself, published, and purchased for sale.

Having purchased weapons with his earned wealth and distributed them among his own people, and having observed his capacity and experience in the handling of military arms, he was honored with the position of Commander-in-Chief, the foremost rank of the democratic republic.
Then the glorious Great War began; he who was opposed to the government came to hear your story, following the proclamation of the January 1, 1925 ordinance regarding the sacrifice of Bismillah.
Overcome by extreme fear at the recitation of that [mantra], the British authority,
observing an opportunity while [the mantra] "He who has the sandals, he has the head" was being uttered on August 25,
1946, was driven out by the power of the treasury.
Proclaimed as a tiger among men who fought alongside the British administration,
he came to hear the account of Bismillah’s sacrifice;
having become enraged at this, a desire for revenge arose within him.
By order of the government, at one time,
Bismillah and twenty-four other revolutionaries were arrested;
they were brought together in a single prison and charged.
Such a most terrifying rebellion was no ordinary event;
hear the account of how Bismillah’s charge for treason arose from his conspiracy against the British rule.

Having been falsely accused of numerous offenses such as robbery and murder, they were deprived of their ten thousand [pieces of wealth]; how then could he have committed an injustice? In the witness statement of the protector, the expenditure for the royal edict was one million.
Having become mad, the rulers have become my enemies;
they have come so that you may hear the story of the sacrifice of Bismillah,
O World-Narayana, and [they have brought] advocates such as Mulla Sadruddin and others.
However, no opposition was ever perceived before Bismillah;
eventually, a few wicked people joined that faction,
as a result of which three others also met their end by the noose around Bismillah's neck.
Furthermore, twenty men were gathered in prison to hear you speak concerning the sacrifice of Bismillah,
as news of this had been circulated among the prisoners.
Then, when a cry of "Alas! Alas! was raised in the midst of the city of Pūrṇa, the leaders of the people made an effort and sent a petition for release out of concern for their welfare;
however, no influence whatsoever was exerted upon Vāyasara.
Not even one person has been released; that sentence of death has arrived for you to hear the account of the sacrifice of Bismillah on the twenty-ninth day of December, in the nineteenth year.
Bismillah! Aṣafāk and Rośanasiṃh—these three men, along with two days prior, Vīra Rājendra Lāhiḍī; those are the killers!
Shame, shame! He who has forgotten us, many as we are, is today the one to be offered as a sacrifice.
For just as the inhabitants of this place, having obtained their independence,
have come to hear the account of the offering of the sacrifice to Bismillah.
